primaryQuery: can you mix Zigbee brands on one hub
readerQuestion: Can I put Zigbee devices from different brands on one hub, and how do I check that each exact model will work before I buy or move it?
selectedBecause: This question recurs across current and long-running r/homeassistant, r/homeautomation, Home Assistant Community, and GitHub device-support discussions. The exact Google result set is fragmented among community answers, brand-specific hub pages, and broad hub explainers that often confuse Zigbee certification with acceptance by a proprietary hub or assume that successful pairing guarantees every feature. Current Home Assistant, Connectivity Standards Alliance, Zigbee2MQTT, ZHA quirks, and vendor documentation supports a durable homeowner answer: mixed brands can share a brand-agnostic coordinator when each exact model is supported, but branded bridges may restrict devices, direct pairing can change features and firmware paths, and one Zigbee device can belong to only one Zigbee network. Search Console has no unowned exact query; all concrete opportunities retain their existing ownerPath, while its established Zigbee and Thread visibility shows adjacent reader interest without authorizing a duplicate URL. This candidate has the broadest recurring setup and buying intent, the clearest weakness in current results, strong local-control relevance, and a distinct boundary from Tara's existing coordinator-software, mesh-repair, Hue-migration, and protocol guides.

searchReview.query: can you mix Zigbee brands on one hub
searchReview.intent: Decide whether one Zigbee hub or coordinator can run devices from several brands, know which kind of hub to choose, verify an exact model before purchase, understand what features may be lost, and consolidate existing hubs without unexpectedly breaking devices or automations.
searchReview.resultGap: Current results frequently collapse three different questions into one: whether devices speak Zigbee, whether a proprietary hub will allow them to join, and whether the selected software exposes every useful function. They rarely give a safe exact-model check across ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT, explain that a successful join may still omit controls or vendor firmware updates, distinguish direct local control from Matter or HomeKit bridge exposure, or warn that a Zigbee device must be reset and leave its old network before joining another. The strongest answer should make those boundaries visible before a purchase or migration.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Zigbee Home Automation documentation
officialSources.supports: ZHA can replace most proprietary Zigbee gateways and create one network for many off-the-shelf devices, but a device can join only one Zigbee network. The documentation also explains exact-model uncertainty, device quirks, coordinator choices, pairing resets, and manufacturer-dependent OTA firmware availability.

officialSources.name: Connectivity Standards Alliance Zigbee overview
officialSources.supports: Zigbee is designed as an interoperable, standards-based low-power mesh; certification is valuable evidence but does not replace checking whether a particular consumer hub and software support an exact model and its manufacturer-specific features.

officialSources.name: Zigbee2MQTT supported-devices database
officialSources.supports: Zigbee2MQTT publishes a searchable model-level compatibility database spanning thousands of products and hundreds of vendors, giving buyers a concrete check rather than a brand-level assumption.

officialSources.name: ZHA device handlers documentation
officialSources.supports: ZHA quirks translate non-standard or manufacturer-specific device behavior into features Home Assistant can understand, explaining why two Zigbee devices can pair but expose different levels of functionality.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Connect ZBT-2 product documentation
officialSources.supports: Connect ZBT-2 is the current official Home Assistant coordinator recommendation for a new ZHA network, and one adapter must be dedicated to either Zigbee or Thread rather than running both protocols at once.

officialSources.name: Third Reality Smart Plug Gen2 product documentation
officialSources.supports: The current Smart Plug Gen2 is a concrete example whose manufacturer lists direct Home Assistant, ZHA, and Zigbee2MQTT support as well as power metering; a separate compatible bridge is needed for other ecosystem paths.

officialSources.name: Third Reality Smart Plug Gen2 current user manual
officialSources.supports: The March 24, 2026 manual identifies the current model as 3RSP03028BZ and explicitly lists Home Assistant through ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT among compatible Zigbee paths.

officialSources.name: Zigbee2MQTT older Third Reality Smart Plug Gen2 model page
officialSources.supports: The public model database separately documents 3RSP02028BZ under the Smart Plug Gen2 name, demonstrating why buyers must not transfer one same-name hardware revision's exposed controls or update evidence to 3RSP03028BZ.

officialSources.name: IKEA DIRIGERA third-party Zigbee help
officialSources.supports: IKEA says third-party Zigbee products may work with DIRIGERA but compatibility and available features can vary, showing why a proprietary brand hub's acceptance policy matters in addition to the radio standard.

officialSources.name: Aqara Door and Window Sensor T1 specifications
officialSources.supports: The exact model DW-S03D is a Zigbee 3.0 sensor, while Aqara's official consumer setup path uses a compatible Aqara hub, illustrating why protocol and vendor-supported path must be recorded separately.

officialSources.name: SONOFF SNZB-02D product documentation
officialSources.supports: The current SNZB-02D is a Zigbee 3.0 temperature and humidity sensor whose documentation identifies compatible gateway requirements and provides an exact model identifier for support checks.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant HomeKit Bridge documentation
officialSources.supports: HomeKit Bridge can share supported Home Assistant controls and readings with Apple Home even when the underlying Zigbee product is not itself a native HomeKit accessory.

officialSources.name: Home Assistant Matter documentation
officialSources.supports: Home Assistant is a Matter controller rather than a Matter bridge. A vendor Matter bridge can expose selected Zigbee child devices, but it does not guarantee that every child or feature will be available.

officialSources.name: Third Reality Smart Bridge MZ1 documentation
officialSources.supports: The MZ1 is Third Reality's documented bridge path for supported Zigbee children to Matter and Apple Home; it is separate from direct ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT pairing.

officialSources.name: Aqara advanced Matter bridging documentation
officialSources.supports: Aqara documents selected hubs as Matter bridges, illustrating that Matter exposure belongs to the compatible bridge path while the child sensor remains Zigbee.

officialSources.name: SONOFF Home Assistant sensor setup guide
officialSources.supports: SONOFF documents the SNZB-02D with both ZHA and Zigbee2MQTT as local Home Assistant paths without a device-maker cloud account.
